No account flag (RD-6 threshold not met).

segment_findings.reason: The driver named the route before leaving the optimal line — 'ok if I go round via Halus Link?' at 10:01 [F7] — and the rider agreed at 10:01 [F8], both preceding the segment start of 10:04 [F3]; this is the RD-5 'agreement before you go' test. Nothing in the record shows the executed track plainly went somewhere other than the named Halus Link corridor (F3 gives only distance/geometry, not a different destination), so the 1.73 km extra is exempt under RD-5. rejected_claims.reason: The off-route segment is real [F3][F1], but RD-1 sends every segment through RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 review and this one is exempt under RD-5 by the driver's pre-departure named-route request and the rider's agreement [F7][F8][RD-1][RD-5]; the existence of the segment alone decides nothing.

Rejected: the fare is a fixed RydeX quote billed on the optimal 9.9 km with 1.0× surge [F4][F5], so no portion of the $23.32 is attributable to the detour mileage, and the billed items are all published [F6][RD-2][FARE-1].

Rejected: RD-6 requires a finding against the driver (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) together with route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; with the segment exempt under RD-5 there is no finding, and the driver's route disputes upheld count is 0 [F15][RD-6].

Not adopted as a determinative ground in the driver's favour beyond RD-5: the RD-4 traffic rationale is unsupported — no incident in the trip window [F12] and only band 4 speeds [F10][F11] — so the exemption rests on RD-5 consent, not on traffic evidence [F9][F10][F11][F12][RD-4][RD-5].
